annotation.title_clean: Decision No. 1412/2023 Issuing the Regulation Governing Unmanned Aircraft Systems (Drones)
annotation.title_en: Decision No. 1412/2023 Issuing the Regulation Governing Unmanned Aircraft Systems (Drones)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Civil Aviation Authority, Sultanate of Oman (Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology)
annotation.summary_en: Omani Civil Aviation Authority decision issuing a binding regulation on drones (including autonomous, AI-preprogrammed aircraft). It requires registration, licensing, insurance and training, sets operating limits and prohibitions, makes licensees liable for damage, and provides fines and licence revocation, with exemptions for military and security agencies.
key_provisions_or_claims: All drones must be registered; flying activities and aerial work require a licence (exemptions for indoor use and toy drones up to 250 g).
Licence conditions: age 18+, third-party liability insurance, exam or training, and an operational permit.
Operations limited to visual line of sight or authorised tracking/collision avoidance, 120 m maximum altitude, no flights within 5 km of airports or protected places without authorisation.
Licensee is liable for damage to persons or property; incidents must be reported immediately.
Fines of 200–600 OMR (doubled for repeat offences) and licence revocation; military and security agencies are exempt.
